strongest_angle: Analyze the Air Accidents Investigation Branch anniversary statement on the EC135 P1 helicopter tail rotor fenestron blade separation near Dingestow, Monmouthshire, detailing the fatigue crack and dye-penetrant findings.

key_facts.fact: On 16 November 2025, an EC135 P1 helicopter with registration G-WPDA experienced an in-flight separation of a tail rotor fenestron blade and landed safely in a field near Dingestow, Monmouthshire.

The UK Air Accidents Investigation Branch stated in its November 16, 2026 anniversary statement that the separated tail rotor blade failed through a fatigue crack, with dye-penetrant found on the crack surfaces.

The Federal Aviation Administration superseded Airworthiness Directive 2024-04-10, which applied to Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH Model EC135P1 helicopters requiring repetitive inspections of specific tail rotor blades for cracks.

quotes.text: The tail rotor blade that separated from EC135 P1 helicopter G-WPDA over Monmouthshire, Wales, a year ago failed through a fatigue crack, and dye-penetrant was found on the crack surfaces.
